A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PACED-RL work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical-reasoning and code-generation experiments, training dynamics, replay ablations, and accuracy-estimator analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds experiments on KL omission, prompt coverage, sampling strategies, and adversarial perturbations.

M1.justification: The training loss, partition network, accuracy approximation, greedy prompt selection, prioritized replay, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The new soft-sampling alternative is evaluated as an ablation rather than incorporated into the proposed PACED-RL procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix C.2 adds MATH-Perturb Simple/Hard pairs to test difficulty estimation under small textual changes that alter problem difficulty. This introduces an adversarial input scenario within mathematical reasoning; the existing training datasets and main evaluation benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: The existing GRPO, FlowRL, DS, LILO, MoPPS, and FlowRL-VarGrad comparisons are retained. v2 additionally compares greedy selection against a soft-sampling alternative at three temperatures in Table 4, and approximate versus full-KL accuracy-estimator selections in Figure 5.

E3.justification: New diagnostic protocols include comparing top-128 selections from 512 prompts every five steps using eight rollouts for KL estimation, measuring distinct-prompt coverage over 150 steps, testing three soft-sampling temperatures, and measuring Simple/Hard pairwise ordering at five checkpoints. Existing training budgets, model sizes, and main benchmark protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendix C.2 substantially expand validation of central design choices: whether dropping KL changes prompt selection, whether greedy selection collapses dataset coverage, whether stochastic selection helps, and whether the estimator detects adversarial difficulty changes. The previous target-accuracy, replay, VarGrad, and correlation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and v2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting procedure. Averaging generated attempts remains distinct from repeated independent training runs.

E6.justification: v2 substantially expands diagnostic results: near-unit selection overlap with 70%/87% KL-estimation latency overhead; 55.7%/62.3% relative prompt coverage; soft-sampling MATH-500 scores of 72.2, 71.4, and 71.8 versus 73.2 for greedy selection; and MATH-Perturb pairwise accuracies of 65.2–69.9%. These are added results under new comparisons, not improvements over v1 scores. Table 1 and the retained benchmark results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Proposition 4.1, the partition-function/accuracy relationship, and both Appendix A derivations are unchanged, including the generalization to arbitrary binary rewards. The additions provide empirical checks and evaluation summaries rather than new proofs, assumptions, or formal guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: interpreting the partition function as an accuracy signal and using it for sample-efficient prompt selection and replay while preserving diversity. The added analyses support these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that difficulty progression prevents narrow prompt-subset collapse and that soft sampling may weaken training by admitting less informative prompts. It also discusses sensitivity to adversarial textual edits and strengthens the practical justification for omitting KL. The existing limitations remain unchanged after renumbering.

D1.justification: Section 5.3 documents implementation details for the new controls, including softmax logits based on estimated accuracy times one minus estimated accuracy, temperature settings, and Monte Carlo KL computation. Appendix B's hardware, optimizers, learning rates, training budgets, preprocessing references, and access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds the MATH-Perturb citation, Huang et al. (2025b), for the new robustness evaluation. Changes to FlowRL, LILO, MoPPS, and other references largely update publication metadata for already cited works; the related-work positioning is otherwise unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized prose revisions, reordered analysis paragraphs, an acknowledgments section, and a new Appendix C.2. The redundant appendix future-work section is removed while its principal directions remain in Section 6. The overall narrative and section structure are preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 5 and Tables 3, 4, and 7, relocates retained displays, and places table captions above tables. The difficulty plot, formerly Figure 5 and now Figure 6, fixes the legend overlap with the step-axis labels while preserving its trends. The overall visual format remains consistent.

improvement.justification: v1 justified KL omission mainly through small estimated KL values; v2 directly checks its effect on prompt selection and quantifies its computational tradeoff. Coverage, sampling, and perturbation tests further support existing design choices and expose estimator sensitivity. These targeted additions improve evidential support, while the main results, theory, and broader limitations concerning model scale and applicability remain unchanged.
